extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, third-party submitters, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and content requirements for (A) requesting redacted publication of a U.S. patent application under 37 CFR 1.217 and (B) third‑party preissuance submissions of printed publications under 35 U.S.C. 122(e) implemented by 37 CFR 1.290. Covers timing, filing medium, required documents, fees, and examiner/office handling rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for redacted publication (37 CFR 1.217)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may request redacted publication eliminating any part or description of the invention that is not also contained in any corresponding applications filed in a foreign country (directly or through a multilateral international agreement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request must be timely (see 16-month timing requirement) and comply with the Office electronic filing system requirements; if not compliant, the Office will publish the full description as provided in 37 CFR 1.215(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for redacted publication request (16-month rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: A redacted copy must be submitted within sixteen (16) months after the earliest filing date for which a benefit is sought under title 35, United States Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 16-month period is statutory (35 U.S.C. 122(b)(2)(B)(v)) and requests for waiver of this period will be denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing compliance for redacted copy
rubrics_metrics.description: The redacted copy of the application must be submitted in compliance with the Office electronic filing system (EFS) requirements; the title in the redacted copy must correspond to the application's title at submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the redacted copy does not comply with EFS requirements, the Office will publish the full description instead of the redacted version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent paper submissions required with redacted EFS filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must concurrently submit in paper (per 37 CFR 1.52(a)) several required items to be filed in the application when submitting a redacted copy electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items required in paper are listed separately (certified foreign copies, translations, marked-up copy, certification). Paper submission is concurrent with EFS filing of the redacted copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copy of corresponding foreign-filed applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A certified copy of each foreign-filed application that corresponds to the U.S. application must be submitted in paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This supports verification that redacted material is only material not present in corresponding foreign applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations and accuracy statement for non-English foreign applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A translation of each foreign-filed application that is in a language other than English must be submitted, together with a statement that the translation is accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translation must be submitted in paper concurrently with the EFS redacted copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marked-up copy showing redactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must submit a marked-up copy of the application showing the redactions in brackets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The marked-up copy is submitted in paper concurrently with the redacted copy filed via EFS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification limiting redactions
rubrics_metrics.description: A certification that the redacted copy eliminates only the part or description of the invention that is not contained in any corresponding foreign-filed application must be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification is required in paper and supports restricted scope of redactions (only material not present in corresponding foreign applications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing fee and certification for redaction-related submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each submission under the procedures for redacted publication must be accompanied by the processing fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(i) and a certification that the redactions are limited to elimination of material relevant only to the part not contained in the redacted copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees apply to submissions described in 37 CFR 1.217(d)(1) and (d)(2); failure to provide required redacted/marked copies in compliance may result in full file wrapper disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing requirement to provide redacted/marked copies upon Office correspondence or applicant submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must, within one month of mailing of any correspondence from the Office, file a copy of such correspondence including any desired redactions and a second copy showing redacted material in brackets; and with each submission by the applicant include similar redacted and bracketed copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each such submission must also be accompanied by the processing fee and the certification that redactions are limited appropriately; failure to comply may result in the Office providing the complete file wrapper to any requester.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redaction submissions not entitled to certificate of mailing
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers submitted for redaction are not entitled to the benefit of the certificate of mailing practice under 37 CFR 1.8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should use applicable mailing or electronic filing methods (e.g., EFS-Web) knowing 1.8 protections do not apply to redaction papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary publication requirements for pre‑November 29, 2000 applications (37 CFR 1.221)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for publication of utility and plant applications filed before November 29, 2000 must include a copy of the application complying with EFS requirements and be accompanied by the publication fee (37 CFR 1.18(d)) and processing fee (37 CFR 1.17(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the request or application copy does not comply, the Office will not publish the application and will refund the publication fee; Office does not intend to publish abandoned applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party submission subject matter (37 CFR 1.290 / 35 U.S.C. 122(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A third party may submit for consideration and entry any patents, published patent applications, or other printed publications of potential relevance to examination of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions under 1.290 are limited to printed publications; protests under 1.291 may include other facts or arguments adverse to patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of third‑party submissions (statutory deadlines)
rubrics_metrics.description: A third‑party submission must be filed prior to the earlier of: (1) the date a notice of allowance under 37 CFR 1.311 is given or mailed, or (2) the later of (i) six months after the application is first published by the Office, or (ii) the date of the first rejection under 37 CFR 1.104 of any claim by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All third-party submissions must be filed prior to, not on, the specified dates; the statutory time periods are not waivable and submissions not timely will be discarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory nature and non-waivability of third‑party timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The time periods in 37 CFR 1.290(b) are statutory and cannot be waived; late submissions will not be entered or considered and will be discarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing as early as possible reduces risk that a non-compliant submission cannot be corrected before the statutory period closes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of RCEs, abandonment, and publications on timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of an RCE does not reset the 1.290(b)(2)(ii) time period; abandonment will not toll the statutory time period for third‑party submissions; earlier WIPO publications do not trigger the Office publication-based six‑month clock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The time period for 1.290(b)(2)(i) is triggered only by publication by the Office; republication under 1.221(b) is not the 'first' publication for 35 U.S.C. 122(e) purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date is date of receipt; holiday/weekend rules apply
rubrics_metrics.description: A third‑party submission is filed on its date of receipt in the Office per 37 CFR 1.6; the holiday/weekend rule of 37 CFR 1.7(a) applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate of mailing/transmission under 37 CFR 1.8 does not apply to 1.290 submissions; USPS Priority Mail Express® per 37 CFR 1.10 and the Office's electronic interface are preferred filing methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content for third‑party submissions (37 CFR 1.290(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each third‑party submission must include: (1) a document list identifying documents or portions submitted; (2) a concise description of the asserted relevance of each item; (3) a legible copy of each item (other than U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications); (4) English translations of any non-English items; and (5) a statement that the party is not an individual with a duty to disclose under 37 CFR 1.56 and that the submission complies with 35 U.S.C. 122(e) and 37 CFR 1.290; plus any required fee or 1.290(g) statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/SB/429 or the Office's web-based interface can be used to prepare the document list and required statements for electronic or paper submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document list formatting and identification requirements (37 CFR 1.290(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The document list must include a heading identifying it as a third‑party submission under 37 CFR 1.290, identify on each page the application number, list U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications in a separate section from other items, and identify each item with specific bibliographic details depending on item type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: U.S. patents: patent number, first named inventor, issue date. U.S. patent application publications: publication number, first named inventor, publication date. Foreign patents/published foreign applications: country/office, applicant/patentee/first named inventor, document number, publication date. Non‑patent publications: author (if any), title, pages submitted, publication date, and where available publisher and place of publication; URLs and evidence of publication required for internet sources and undated items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial-document listing permitted when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: When a lengthy document contains both relevant and irrelevant material, a third party may identify only the relevant portion (e.g., one chapter) instead of the entire document where practical; otherwise identify the entire document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps focus the examiner on the potentially relevant portions and reduce unnecessary material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and fee exemptions for third‑party submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: A fee (37 CFR 1.17(o)) is required for every ten items or fraction thereof identified in the document list, except no fee is required for a submission listing three or fewer total items that is accompanied by a statement that, after reasonable inquiry, the submission is the first and only submission under 35 U.S.C. 122(e) filed in the application by the party or a party in privity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/SB/429 allows indicating whether a fee is due or selecting the 'first and only' statement where the fee exemption applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner/office handling of non‑compliant or inappropriate third‑party communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Office personnel are instructed not to reply to or act upon third‑party inquiries or submissions except those in compliance with 37 CFR 1.290 or 37 CFR 1.291; oral or telephone comments from third parties are declined and non‑compliant submissions will not be entered and will be discarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncompliant submissions, or submissions not provided for in the rules, may be referred to the Office of Enrollment and Discipline if filed by registered practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between third‑party submissions (1.290) and protests (1.291)
rubrics_metrics.description: Third‑party submissions under 37 CFR 1.290 are limited to printed publications and require a concise description of asserted relevance. Protests under 37 CFR 1.291 may include facts or information adverse to patentability and arguments, and require a 'concise explanation of the relevance' that may include arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the correct procedure: 1.290 for submitting printed publications for consideration in the record; 1.291 for protests that include arguments or other information adverse to patentability (but protests are subject to applicant consent after publication per 35 U.S.C. 122(c)).
